paper_id: LONGCODEU_ Benchmarking Long-Context Language Models on Long Code Understanding
title: LONGCODEU: Benchmarking Long-Context Language Models on Long Code Understanding
motivation: Progress in long-context LMs is hampered by absence of rigorous evaluation framework for long code understanding
problem_framing: Long code understanding requires four aspects: unit perception, intra-unit understanding, inter-unit relation, and documentation understanding
key_insight: LCLMs' performance drops dramatically when length exceeds 32K, far short of claimed 128K-1M context windows
method_signature: Benchmark with 8 tasks across 4 understanding aspects, 3,983 examples, 0-128K token lengths
evaluation_criteria: Recall/precision metrics with EM, LCS, CodeBLEU, BLEU adapted to task granularity
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: LCLMs fail to model code context effectively in their claimed context windows; inter-code unit relation understanding is most challenging
evidence_for_taste: inter-code unit relation understanding is the most challenging
performance drops dramatically when the long code length is greater than 32K
LCLMs fail to model code context effectively
falls far short of their claimed 128K~1M context windows
near to 10 or even close to 0 on some tasks
thinking_moves: Identified 5 fundamental limitations in existing benchmarks to justify new evaluation
Created hierarchical taxonomy of 4 understanding aspects from real-world software tasks
Distinguished code understanding from memorization by testing w/o context
Designed task-specific metrics aligned to output granularity
Used Kendall-Tau τ ≥ 0.75 to validate metric reliability against human evaluation
